seoDescription: Learn how to add polished, performant page transitions to SvelteKit sites using the page store, layout props, key blocks, built-in transitions (fly), and custom CSS-based transition functions. This tutorial covers detecting navigations, preventing overlapping in/out animations, mapping transition direction to transform-origin, creating reusable transition components, and typing custom transitions in TypeScript for scalable, production-ready UI animations.

chapters.description: Prevent in/out overlap by using separate in/out configs, delays, and tweak durations and directions for smooth transitions.

chapters.description: Create a custom Svelte transition function that returns a CSS animation and use easing and transform-origin for polished effects.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Page detection**: Use the **$page** store from SvelteKit to inspect route IDs and URL pathname for navigation information.

- **Mounting/unmounting pages**: Wrap your page slot with a **key** block keyed by route ID or pathname to destroy and recreate page components when navigation occurs.

- **Transitions**: Use built-in Svelte transitions (for example, **fly**) and configure **in** and **out** separately to avoid overlapping animations.

- **Avoid overlap**: Prevent simultaneous in/out animations by delaying the intro (in) animation by the out duration, or by using a parent layout to know the next route in advance.

- **Custom transitions**: Implement a custom transition function that returns a transition object with **delay**, **duration**, **easing**, and a **css(t)** function; Svelte will generate a CSS animation for performance.

- **Easings**: Apply easing functions (e.g., **cubicIn**, **elasticOut**) to the 0→1 time parameter to shape animation timing.

- **Directional origin mapping**: Use the provided **direction** ('in', 'out', 'both') to map to **transform-origin** (e.g., left→right) for context-aware animations.

- **Reusable components**: Abstract transitions into a reusable **PageTransition** component that accepts **key**, **duration**, and other props to centralize animation logic.

- **TypeScript types**: Type your custom transition with **Params** and **Options** (including direction) and return a **TransitionConfig** so editors provide correct typings for T and U.

> [!TIP] Use layout-level load() to expose the upcoming pathname as a prop so transitions know about navigation ahead of time.

> [!NOTE] The css(t) in custom transitions receives t in [0,1]; apply easing functions to t for advanced timing behavior.

> [!IMPORTANT] Always separate in/out settings or add appropriate delays to prevent the outgoing page from overlapping the incoming page animation.
